$comment: Riftlight, Wandering Sky key node (docs/campaigns/continental-rift/arc.md, the-island-due-back; design note island-continuity-review.md). Rewritten in November 2026 to the Borrowed Ruins pilot's bar. Question: why has the island come back early? Keeper Juniper carries it with Pip Thistledown and Tumble the courier. The p1 (mooring_stone) is the Sky fragment: the stone shows the land below in an older shape. Reads whales_guided / whales_scattered; sets island_messages_saved, island_warning_sent and island_relay_delayed for squall-temple, and fragment_sky_learned on every success path.
title: The Island Due Back

plate.narration: Beneath the clouds, a low island comes into view. A notch breaks its flat brow. On the lookout, a bell waits beside folded signal cloths and a landing board.

goal.text: Why has the island come back early?

steps.label: Spot the island in the clouds
Send word to the temple ahead

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny and a little spooky, with real consequences. Short sentences. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel. The island is old and tired, not dangerous; nobody dies.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Keeper Juniper: Keeper Juniper, the kitsune island keeper (she/her). Brisk, warm and practical; sings instructions, keeps the island songs on a scroll tied to her tail, talks to islands as if they can hear. Wants Notchbrow home safe and to know why it came early.
npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Young manticore scout (he/him). Eager, notebook always out, quotes "Lady Olivia says..." and tries her ideas. Wants to impress her. Kind underneath; changes his mind when the party gives him a reason.
npcVoices.Tumble: Tumble, a young griffin island courier (she/her). Fast, cheerful and terrible at landing; carries letters and messages between the islands. Owes the party if they save her letters.

arrival.narration: Past the whales' turning place, a bell hangs on a post at the very edge of the sky. Keeper Juniper, the kitsune island keeper, rings it with her tail. Pip Thistledown, the young manticore scout, is here too, notebook out. "An old island called Notchbrow is coming home!" Juniper calls. "Our songs have waited for it. But it's early. A whole year early! Why has the island come back early? Help me find out before it drifts past."

variants.text: Far out, the whales you guided clear swim ahead of something big in the clouds.
The whale lane is empty. Since the folds were forced open early, the whales have scattered.

due_song.narration: Juniper unrolls a long song-scroll, tied to her tail so the wind can't steal it. "Every drifting island has a song for its road," she says. "Notchbrow's road is a grandmother long. The last line says: never early, never late." She frowns. "It has never once been early." Pip writes NEVER EARLY and underlines it. "Lady Olivia says early is always better," he says. "Not for islands," says Juniper.

spot.narration: Clouds roll past like sheep. Somewhere inside them, an island is coming. "I need to know which side it will touch," says Juniper, "so the landing board is waiting there." She hands out two sighting sticks with notches cut in them. Pip points his spoon at the bell tower. "Lady Olivia says always get up high!"

variants.text: Out in the clouds, the whales bend their lane into a long, slow curve. "They're swimming around something," Juniper whispers.
Juniper looks for the whales anyway. "They always swim ahead of a returning island," she says quietly. "Today we only have our eyes."

check_tower.narration: The bell tower is a ladder with big ideas. It sways. The bell bonks you on the head, gently. "Sorry," Juniper tells the bell.
check_tower.prompt: Climb the swaying tower and spot the island in the clouds

onSuccess.narration: From the top you see it: a gray shape in the clouds, coming in on the right. Juniper drags the landing board over to the right side.

onFailure.narration: The tower sways, and so does the whole sky. You point left. Everyone runs left. It was not left.

check_sticks.narration: Line up two notches with the cloud where the island hides, and you know its road. If only the clouds would hold still.
check_sticks.prompt: Line up the sighting sticks on the hidden island

onSuccess.narration: The notches line up. "Right side!" says Juniper, and drags the landing board over.

onFailure.narration: A cloud drifts and fools the sticks. You call left. Everyone runs left. It was not left.

whales_lead.narration: The whales swim their long curve, slow and sure, like a line drawn across the sky. At the end of it, the clouds part. "Right side!" Juniper laughs. "Thank you, whales." She lays the landing board on the right, first try. Pip writes WHALES KNOW THINGS in very big letters.

fly_look.narration: Your griffin climbs above the clouds. From up there you can see the island's whole road: a long gray shape, coming in on the right. You glide back down and point. Juniper drags the landing board over. "Show-off," says Pip, deeply impressed.

wrong_side.narration: Juniper laid the landing board on the left. The island is coming in on the right! The board is long and very, very heavy. "Quick," says Juniper. "Before it slides past!"
wrong_side.prompt: Drag the heavy landing board along the edge to the right side

onSuccess.narration: You drag it across, scraping and puffing, just in time.

onFailure.narration: The board bucks and lands on a toe. You get it there, just. Juniper wraps the toe in her scarf.

spotted.narration: Out of the clouds slides an island: low and grassy, with a notch in its flat brow. Notchbrow. An old stone stands near its edge. Then your Listening Chime hums in your pack and tips, all by itself, toward the glacier far behind you. Juniper's ears go flat. "Islands drift," she says slowly. "They don't get pulled."

variants.text: A young whale drifts past alone, calling for its family. Pip watches it go and chews his pencil. "Lady Olivia said they'd be fine," he says.

tumble.narration: Thump! A griffin lands beside you in a heap, mailbag first. "Tumble," she says, upside down. "Island courier. I carry everyone's letters between the islands, and any message you like. I'm very fast. I'm just bad at stopping." She squints at Notchbrow. "That one's early. I haven't got a single letter for it."

gust.narration: Then a gust howls over the lookout. Tumble's mailbag bursts, and letters fly up like startled birds. At the same moment, Juniper's signal frame tips toward the edge. It is the tall frame she flashes cloth messages from. "My letters!" "My frame!" There is only time to save one.

check_letters.narration: Letters swirl all around the lookout. One says: For my grandma, third island on the left. Tumble flaps after them, mostly sideways.
check_letters.prompt: Snatch the flying letters out of the wind

onSuccess.narration: You catch every letter, even the one for grandma. Behind you, the signal frame topples, and its pole cracks.

onFailure.narration: You catch a handful. The rest sail into a wet cloud and come out soggy. Behind you, the signal frame topples, and its pole cracks.

check_frame.narration: The frame is tall and wobbly, with two cloth flags on top. Its feet are sliding toward nothing at all.
check_frame.prompt: Haul the tipping signal frame back from the edge

onSuccess.narration: You haul it back and stamp its feet into the grass. It stands. Behind you, Tumble's letters sail into a wet cloud and come out soggy.

onFailure.narration: It slips through your hands, and its pole cracks on the rocks. Behind you, Tumble's letters sail into a wet cloud and come out soggy.

gust_after.narration: Pip writes it all down. "Lady Olivia says a good scout saves the most important thing," he says. "Which one was it?"

variants.text: Tumble hugs her dry mailbag. "I owe you," she says. "Need a message carried? Anything at all?"
Tumble pegs her soggy letters on the bell rope like washing. "No flying till they're dry," she sighs. "Wet letters stick to my feathers."
Juniper pats the frame. "Good. With this, I can flash a message to any island I can see."
Juniper looks at the cracked frame. "No flashing messages until that's mended," she says.

crossing.narration: Notchbrow slides up beside the lookout, close enough to smell its grass. Juniper pushes out the landing board. It reaches, just. The gap breathes: wide, narrow, wide. "Cross when it's narrow," she says. "And don't look down. Down is mostly cloud." Tumble stays behind to mind the lookout.

choices.label: Walk the board when the gap is narrow
Crawl across, holding the side ropes
Step on the whales' low note

check_walk.narration: The board bounces with every step. Pip walks behind you with his notebook in his teeth.
check_walk.prompt: Walk the bouncing board across while the gap is narrow

onSuccess.narration: You step onto soft grass. Pip hops down after you and takes the notebook out of his teeth. "Ptoo."

onFailure.narration: The gap opens wide and the board drops. You hang on by your fingers while Pip grabs your collar and pulls. You're up! But Pip's notebook falls out of his teeth and down into the clouds.

check_crawl.narration: You crawl across like a caterpillar, gripping the side ropes. The board tilts. The ropes creak.
check_crawl.prompt: Crawl the tilting board and hold on tight when it lurches

onSuccess.narration: Slow and sure, you roll onto the grass. Pip crawls after you and says caterpillars are underrated.

onFailure.narration: The board lurches. You hold the ropes while your legs swing over nothing, until Pip hauls you up by your pack. His notebook slides out of his pocket and away into the clouds.

whale_note.narration: Far below, a whale sings one low note each time the island swings closest. "Listen," says Juniper. "Step on the note."

interaction.cue: Step onto the board on the whale's low note.

onSuccess.narration: Boom, goes the whale, and you step. The board barely moves. "They're helping," Juniper says softly.

onFailure.narration: You step a beat late, and the board wobbles under you. Back you hop. You'll have to cross the ordinary way.

onAssisted.narration: Juniper hums along with the whale, and you all step on the note together.

leap.narration: Your duskrunner backs up, runs and leaps the gap with a rope. You tie it off on a crooked tree, and everyone crosses hand over hand. Pip arrives last, upside down. "On purpose," he says.

on_island.narration: Notchbrow is old. Its grass is soft, its trees are crooked, and a scarecrow wears a hat nobody has worn in a hundred years. A hen pops out of a bush and glares at you. She has been riding this island all alone, and she does not like visitors. Juniper kneels and pats the grass. "Welcome home, old thing. Now, why are you early?"

variants.text: Pip pats his empty pocket. "All my Lady Olivia notes," he says sadly. The hen sits on his foot.

pip_hen.narration: Pip scoops up the hen before anyone can stop him. "A sample!" he says. "Lady Olivia will love her. A real hen from an island that came home early!" The hen does not love Pip. She pecks his hat and stares, very hard, at her bush. Juniper raises an eyebrow. "She lives here," she says.

choices.label: Put the hen back in her bush

hen_kept.narration: Pip tucks the hen inside his scarf, so only her head pokes out. She glares at you all the way, and every few steps she twists around to look back at her bush. "She'll get used to me," says Pip. The hen does not look like a hen who gets used to things.

hen_left.narration: Pip sighs and sets the hen down by her bush. She fluffs up to twice her size, and then follows him anyway, pecking at his heels. "I think she likes me," says Pip. "I think she's making sure you leave," says Juniper.

explore.narration: "The oldest songs say Notchbrow has a mooring stone," says Juniper, "where it tied up long ago, with words carved on it. Nobody alive has read them." Two ways lead toward the stone: a path through the crooked orchard, or the high ridge above it.

choices.label: Find the path through the orchard

check_orchard.narration: The orchard paths all look alike. The trees lean every which way, as if they are listening for something.
check_orchard.prompt: Find the old path through the crooked orchard

onSuccess.narration: You spot old stepping stones under the grass. They lead straight there.

onFailure.narration: Around and around, through the brambles. You pass the same scarecrow three times. The third time, the hen is sitting on its hat.

check_ridge.narration: The ridge is narrow and windy. On one side, grass. On the other side, a very long way down to the clouds.
check_ridge.prompt: Hurry along the windy ridge without slipping

onSuccess.narration: You run the ridge and hop down beside the stone.

onFailure.narration: A gust shoves you. You slide down the grassy side on your back, all the way to the stone, and stop with a thump.

lost_orchard.narration: At last the hen gets bored. She hops off the scarecrow and marches away, and Pip follows her, because nobody has a better idea. She leads you straight to the stone and settles on top of it like a crown. "She knew the way all along," says Juniper. You have lost time, and Notchbrow has drifted on.

stone.narration: The mooring stone is taller than Juniper, with a round eye worn smooth by a rope, long ago. Shapes are carved all over it, under the moss. Juniper brushes the moss away with her tail, very gently. "Copy it," she says, "before the island turns and the light slides off it."

variants.text: Pip opens his notebook and licks his pencil.
Pip has no notebook now, so he holds the moss back for you instead.

copy.narration: Juniper hums each carved shape as the sun finds it, one at a time. Watch the shapes, then draw them in order, before the island turns them into shadow.

interaction.cue: Watch the carved shapes, then draw them in order.

onSuccess.narration: You draw every shape before the light moves on. Juniper stops humming. "That's all of it."

onFailure.narration: The island turns. The last shapes slide into shadow, around the far side of the stone!

onAssisted.narration: Pip calls out each shape as Juniper hums it, and you draw them together.

check_chase.narration: The island is turning slowly, and the stone's shadow turns with it. The last carvings are sliding around the far side.
check_chase.prompt: Run around the turning stone and copy the last shapes before they go dark

onSuccess.narration: Around and around you go, and you catch every shape. Juniper claps.

onFailure.narration: You trip over a root, and then over the hen. By the time you're up, your copy is a scribble, but you saw every shape.

mooring_stone.narration: You hold your copy up beside the stone, and suddenly you see it. The carving is a map. Not of the sky: of the land far below. Hills, a river, a long coast. But the hills are in the wrong places, and the river runs another way. This stone shows the land below in an older shape, the way it lay long ago. It doesn't match Master Orin's map. It matches something older.

pull.narration: Then your Listening Chime swings out of your pack on its strap and points, hard, toward the glacier where all this began. It tugs like a puppy on a leash. Pip has to hold it with both paws. All around you, Notchbrow creaks the same way. Juniper stares toward the glacier. "So that's why it's early," she whispers. "It isn't coming home. Something is pulling it."

hold.narration: Notchbrow lurches toward the glacier, away from the lookout. Across the gap, the landing board scrapes and slides. Pip grabs his long coil of rope. "Lady Olivia says if something's being pulled, pull back! Tie the island to the lookout, through the stone's eye!" Juniper shakes her head. "A rope that holds an island pulls on everything it's tied to. Let it go its way, and run for the board."

choices.label: Tie the island to the lookout
Let it go, and run for the board

check_tie.narration: You thread the rope through the stone's old eye. Pip throws the other end across the gap, and by pure luck it loops around the bell post. Everyone pulls. The island groans like an old bed.
check_tie.prompt: Haul the rope tight and hold the island still

onSuccess.narration: The knot holds. Notchbrow stops with a shudder.

onFailure.narration: The rope burns through your hands before it catches. Notchbrow stops with a jerk that knocks you flat.

tied.narration: Notchbrow stops. Under your hands, the mooring stone creaks, and a thin crack runs through its eye. Juniper puts a paw on it. "Shh," she tells it. "Only a little while." Pip's ears go down. "Lady Olivia never said what the rope does to the other end."

variants.text: Across the gap, the rope pulls tight over the lookout and sweeps Juniper's signal frame flat. Crack. It won't flash anything now.
Across the gap, the rope pulls tight over the lookout and drags the cracked signal frame through the grass.

walk_back.narration: Held still, the board is easy. You walk back across like it's a garden path, and the hen comes too, tucked under Pip's arm. Then the rope begins to sing, a low, worried hum. "It won't hold," says Juniper. "Nothing holds against a pull like that."

check_snap.narration: The rope stretches thin as a noodle. The bell post leans. Everyone grabs something.
check_snap.prompt: Hold on to the bell post as the rope gives way

onSuccess.narration: Twang! The rope snaps and whips away. You hang on, and the lookout stays in one piece. Notchbrow lurches off, faster than before.

onFailure.narration: Twang! The rope snaps and the bell post wobbles. You go rolling into the grass, and the bell bonks down beside you. Notchbrow lurches off, faster than before.

run_back.narration: You run. The board is sliding off the island's edge, a little at a time. On the lookout, Juniper braces the near end with all four paws.

choices.label: Let Tumble fly you a line

variants.text: Tumble is already flapping. "I can fly you a line!" she shouts. "But then I'll be too puffed to carry anything else for a while."

check_return.narration: The board tips like a seesaw. Pip runs beside you with the hen under one arm.
check_return.prompt: Race across the sliding board before it falls

onSuccess.narration: You hit the lookout running. Behind you, the board slides off Notchbrow's edge, and Juniper hauls it in.

onFailure.narration: The board drops under your feet. You leap the last bit and land in a heap, and the board tumbles away into the clouds. "I have another one," says Juniper. "Somewhere."

check_swing.narration: Notchbrow swings toward the lookout and away, toward and away, like a slow door in the wind. Juniper counts with you from the far side.
check_swing.prompt: Count the island's swings and jump on the closest one

onSuccess.narration: Three, two, one, jump! The gap is only a hop, and you land in Juniper's arms. Pip lands on Juniper's tail.

onFailure.narration: You jump a beat late. The gap is wider than a hop, and you land half on the lookout and half on nothing, until Juniper hauls you up by the pack.

tumble_line.narration: Tumble swoops across with the end of a rope in her beak, and you cross holding it, safe and steady. Then she lands, hard, on the lookout. "Ow," she says. "Fine. I'm fine." She is puffed right out. She will need a long rest before she can carry anything again.

back.narration: Back on the lookout, you watch Notchbrow go. It drifts away across the sky, still leaning toward the glacier. Juniper counts everyone twice, and the hen three times. Pip sits down hard. "We read an island," he says. "Nobody is going to believe me."

variants.text: The broken rope trails from the stone's eye like a tail.

Then the hen wriggles out of Pip's scarf, flaps across the gap with a furious squawk and lands on Notchbrow's grass, home. Pip stares after her. "She just wanted to go home," he says. "Moved things do that," says Juniper.

drift_on.narration: Far ahead, right in Notchbrow's path, a temple island sits on a cloud, all red roofs and bells. A gray squall is rolling in behind it. Juniper's tail goes stiff. "That's a temple called the Squall Temple," she says, "where the keepers ring the weather bells. Notchbrow will drift right into them, in a storm." Your chime still leans toward the glacier, steady as a compass.

rest.narration: Juniper pours ginger tea from a pot shaped like a whale. Pip drinks his in one gulp and burns his tongue. The hen drinks from the lid. "The temple must hear from us before the island gets there," says Juniper. "A warning would send them all inside to get their push poles ready. Our welcome song would bring them out to clear the landing and let it rest. A song rings fast from bell to bell. A warning needs a carrier."

warn.narration: Juniper writes it fast: An island is coming. Go inside. Get your push poles ready. Pip adds a drawing of a very worried face. "Now," says Juniper, "who can carry it in time?"

welcome.narration: Juniper smiles. "An old island coming home should be greeted, not pushed." She tunes the bell with her tail. Pip looks at the squall. "Greeted? Out in that?" "They'll have lanterns," says Juniper.

dispatch.narration: "Quick is best," says Juniper. "Notchbrow won't wait for us." A young keeper is already lacing her boots, ready to run it along the stepping islands. That will be slow, but sure.

choices.label: Flash it from the signal frame
Send it along the stepping islands

variants.text: Tumble is snoring on the bell post, worn out from flying your line.
Tumble's letters are still dripping on the bell rope.
The signal frame lies cracked in the grass.

by_tumble.narration: Tumble tucks the warning in with her dry letters. "Squall Temple. Easy. It's big and it rings." She takes off, wobbles once and is gone into the clouds. A moment later you hear a faraway thump. "She's landed," says Juniper. "Somewhere."

by_frame.narration: Juniper flashes the cloths: white, striped, white, faster than you can blink. Far away, a tiny light flashes back from the temple's tower. "They have it," she says, "with time to spare."

by_hand.narration: The young keeper runs off along the stepping islands with the warning in her paw, hopping from rock to rock. She is quick, but the islands are far apart, and Notchbrow is quicker. "It will get there," says Juniper. "Late, but it will get there."

welcome_rung.narration: Juniper rings the welcome song on her bell. Far away, the next island's bell rings it back, and the next, and the next, all the way to the temple. Songs travel fast in the sky. "They'll clear the landing and come out to greet it," Juniper says happily. Pip looks at the squall and says nothing, very loudly.

farewell.narration: Pip turns his spoon over and over. "Lady Olivia says if something wanders, you tie it down," he says. "But Notchbrow wasn't wandering, was it? It was being pulled. Was she wrong?"

variants.text: He looks at the cracked stone, far away now. "And the rope broke the stone."

pip_doubt.narration: Pip thinks about it for a long time. Then he writes on a scrap of Juniper's paper: Ask first. Tie later. Maybe. He folds it very small. "Don't tell her I wrote maybe," he says.

pip_loyal.narration: Pip nods hard. "She is," he says. "She always is." But he keeps looking toward the glacier, where your chime points, and the tip of his tail twitches.

ending.narration: Juniper adds a new line to her song-scroll: Came home early. Pulled. "Follow Notchbrow to the temple, if you can," she says. "They'll need help when it gets there. Or the whales' turning place is always open to you." So here is your piece: an island was pulled across the sky, and its old stone shows the land below in an older shape. Something is moving the land. What is it? And can you put things right?

variants.text: The stone's eye is cracked, and a broken rope trails behind Notchbrow.
Your warning is still hopping along the stepping islands, a long way behind the island.
Pip waves from the bell post, his folded note safe in his pocket.
Pip waves from the bell post, already planning what to tell Lady Olivia.
You carry another piece too. Master Orin Vale will want to lay them side by side.
You carry another piece too. Master Orin Vale will want to lay them side by side.
